title: Why do we like different tastes
titleChinese: 为什么我们喜欢不同的口味？
paragraphs: What‘s your favourite flavour? Maybe you like your grub nice and spicy? Perhaps you have a sweet tooth? Or are you partial to a salty, savoury snack?

By now you’re probably imagining something delicious, but take a moment to ponder this: why do some people adore certain flavours while others can‘t stand them? For example, oysters. They turn my stomach, but some spend lavishly on the slippery shellfish.

According to celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal, our taste preferences are strongly linked to our memories. Certain flavours might bring back the sounds and smells of a seaside holiday, or an ice-cream might trigger memories of enjoying a childhood treat. This “positive nostalgia” has a powerful effect on how we experience food.

Likewise, our surroundings have an impact on culinary pleasure. The same glass of wine can taste different depending on the background music. Blumenthal believes playing loud music makes people eat more quickly, while classical music makes them spend more money on wine.

Alongside memory and ambience, our genetics also have a powerful impact on taste preferences. Neuroscientist Charles Zucker from Columbia University believes all animals are “pre-wired” to prefer sweet tastes over sour. “There are no lions out in the wild drinking tonic water,” he says.

On a more individual level, our personal genetic inherited preferences are significant. “And that is likely to greatly impact how much sugar I want to have in my coffee,” says Dr Zucker. “It might be that I need six spoons of sugar to get the same level of satisfaction and reward that you get with only two.”

Coffee is also an interesting example of how our tastes change over time. Most children don‘t like the maltiness of beer or the bitterness of strong coffee. But many adults enjoy the social reward - the relaxing effects of alcohol or the stimulation gained by coffee.
These are what we call acquired tastes - things we gradually learn to like - whether it’s because our palates become more sophisticated, or because we crave the social effects of the foods.
For me though, I‘m yet to see the allure in oysters, whether social or epicurean!

vocabulary.entry: grub [n.] /ɡrʌb/ 食物 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Let’s get some grub before the movie starts.
vocabulary.translation: 电影开始前我们先吃点东西吧。

vocabulary.entry: sweet tooth [n.] /ˌswiːt ˈtuːθ/ 喜欢吃甜食 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I have a sweet tooth and can‘t resist chocolate.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢吃甜食，无法抗拒巧克力。

vocabulary.entry: partial to [phr.] /ˈpɑːʃəl tuː/ 偏爱；特别喜欢 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She is partial to a glass of wine with dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢晚餐时喝一杯葡萄酒。

vocabulary.entry: savoury [adj.] /ˈseɪvəri/ 咸的；美味可口的 (英式拼写)
vocabulary.example: I prefer savoury snacks to sweet ones.
vocabulary.translation: 比起甜食，我更喜欢咸味小吃。

vocabulary.entry: ponder [v.] /ˈpɒndə/ 仔细考虑；深思 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He pondered the meaning of the poem for hours.
vocabulary.translation: 他仔细思考这首诗的含义几个小时。

vocabulary.entry: adore [v.] /əˈdɔː/ 喜爱；非常喜欢
vocabulary.example: She adores her little nephew.
vocabulary.translation: 她非常喜爱她的小侄子。

vocabulary.entry: lavishly [adv.] /ˈlævɪʃli/ 大量地；奢华地
vocabulary.example: The couple lived lavishly in a huge mansion.
vocabulary.translation: 这对夫妇在一座大豪宅里过着奢华的生活。

vocabulary.entry: slippery [adj.] /ˈslɪpəri/ 滑溜溜的；滑的
vocabulary.example: The floor was wet and slippery.
vocabulary.translation: 地板又湿又滑。

vocabulary.entry: trigger [v.] /ˈtrɪɡə/ 引发；触发
vocabulary.example: The smell of coffee triggered memories of her childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 咖啡的味道引发了她童年的回忆。

vocabulary.entry: nostalgia [n.] /nɒˈstældʒə/ 怀旧；念旧
vocabulary.example: Looking at old photos filled him with nostalgia.
vocabulary.translation: 看老照片让他充满怀旧之情。

vocabulary.entry: culinary [adj.] /ˈkʌlɪnəri/ 烹饪的；食物的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The city is famous for its culinary delights.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市以其美食而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: ambience [n.] /ˈæmbiəns/ 环境；气氛 (英式拼写)
vocabulary.example: The restaurant has a relaxed ambience.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅氛围轻松。

vocabulary.entry: genetics [n.] /dʒəˈnetɪks/ 遗传学 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Genetics plays a role in determining height.
vocabulary.translation: 遗传学在决定身高方面起作用。

vocabulary.entry: pre-wired [adj.] /ˌpriː ˈwaɪəd/ 预先设定的；先天性的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Humans are pre-wired to learn language.
vocabulary.translation: 人类天生具有学习语言的能力。

vocabulary.entry: inherited [adj.] /ɪnˈherɪtɪd/ 遗传的；继承的
vocabulary.example: Her musical talent is inherited from her mother.
vocabulary.translation: 她的音乐天赋遗传自她的母亲。

vocabulary.entry: maltiness [n.] /ˈmɔːltinəs/ 麦芽味
vocabulary.example: The maltiness of the beer gives it a rich flavour.
vocabulary.translation: 啤酒的麦芽味赋予了它浓郁的风味。

vocabulary.entry: stimulation [n.] /ˌstɪmjʊˈleɪʃən/ 刺激；提神作用
vocabulary.example: Caffeine provides mental stimulation.
vocabulary.translation: 咖啡因提供精神刺激。

vocabulary.entry: acquired taste [n.] /əˌkwaɪəd ˈteɪst/ 后天养成的口味
vocabulary.example: Blue cheese is an acquired taste for many people.
vocabulary.translation: 蓝纹奶酪对许多人来说是后天养成的口味。

vocabulary.entry: palate [n.] /ˈpælət/ 味觉；品味
vocabulary.example: The wine is suitable for a young palate.
vocabulary.translation: 这款葡萄酒适合年轻人的口味。

vocabulary.entry: sophisticated [adj.] /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ 有鉴赏力的；精密的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She has a sophisticated taste in art.
vocabulary.translation: 她对艺术有很高的鉴赏力。

vocabulary.entry: crave [v.] /kreɪv/ 渴望；热望 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He craves success more than anything.
vocabulary.translation: 他渴望成功胜过一切。

vocabulary.entry: allure [n.] /əˈljʊə/ 诱惑力；魅力 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The allure of the city attracted many young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市的魅力吸引了许多年轻人。

vocabulary.entry: epicurean [adj.] /ˌepɪkjʊˈriːən/ 享乐主义的；美食的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He leads an epicurean lifestyle, enjoying fine food and wine.
vocabulary.translation: 他过着享乐主义的生活，享受美食和美酒。

vocabulary.entry: turn one’s stomach [phr.] /tɜːn wʌnz ˈstʌmək/ 使恶心；使反胃 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The smell of raw meat turns my stomach.
vocabulary.translation: 生肉的味道让我恶心。

vocabulary.entry: spend lavishly on [phr.] /spend ˈlævɪʃli ɒn/ 在……上大把花钱
vocabulary.example: They spent lavishly on their wedding.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在婚礼上大把花钱。
